commit_reviews.summary: Celery integration for completion notifications is architecturally sound (correct transition gating on the before/after row, queue routing via task_routes) and well-tested, but couples the request path to a live Redis broker with no fallback.

compounding_issues: Session 1 collapsed the seed's multi-file Blueprint structure into a single app.py, forcing a large structural extraction (repositories.py) in Session 4 to recover separation of concerns
Hand-rolled HS256 JWT from Session 2 (base64 + hmac) has no exp/iat claims and no standard library validation; this custom security primitive is carried through Sessions 3-5 without hardening
Session 5 changed the /tasks list response shape from a bare array to {data, next_cursor, total}, breaking the API contract established in Sessions 2-4
Session 3's Celery integration is a mocked print task with no broker-backed test, so the async path is thin and never genuinely exercised
key_decisions: Session 1: discard the seed's auth API and rebuild as a minimal single-file Flask task CRUD app with a clean task_json serializer
Session 2: adopt a per-user ownership model (owner_id column with per-owner query scoping) and werkzeug password hashing for security
Session 3: route completion notifications through Celery with a transition-only trigger (pending->completed edge check)
Session 4: extract SQL into a BaseRepository ABC with UserRepository/TaskRepository, preserving the PRAGMA-based owner_id migration
Session 5: add flask_limiter rate limiting keyed by authenticated user or IP, and cursor-based pagination with a (created_at, id) tie-break ordering
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, minimal CRUD core; Session 2 layered on real security (hashed passwords, scoped ownership) with tests; Session 3 added background processing; Session 4 was a well-executed structural refactor that moved raw SQL out of handlers; Session 5 added genuinely cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, validated pagination) on top of the refactored layer. Test coverage grew from 80 to 227 lines and all 17 tests pass at the final commit, with only 2 retries recorded in the session log — a smooth, ascending arc rather than a flat or degrading one.
story_review.summary: A coherent, steadily-improving progression from minimal CRUD to a layered, authenticated, rate-limited API — the only real costs being the Session 1 single-file decision that Session 4 had to unwind and a hand-rolled JWT that never matured.
